name: Grant Writing Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on grant writing so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on grant writing so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any grant writing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Before starting grant writing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
3. Keep grant writing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. When grant writing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
5. When grant writing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. State assumptions about grant writing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen grant writing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. Prefer the simplest grant writing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
9. Check that grant writing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
10. Document any non-obvious grant writing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
11. Keep grant writing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic grant writing advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of grant writing correctness.
- Avoid introducing new grant writing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting grant writing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop grant writing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about grant writing over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
